summary.intent: The user wanted to create and push a copy of the repo to their GitHub account, configure Entire.io/Codex logging for it, and verify that session/checkpoint data appears on the Entire web UI for the new repo.
summary.outcome: The repo was created and pushed as stale2000/git-sync, Entire/Codex hooks were installed and trusted, multiple checkpoints were created and pushed to the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch, and a real Codex CLI session was captured. The Entire web UI still did not list checkpoints despite authenticated browser access and verified raw checkpoint files on GitHub.

repo: Target repo was corrected from stale2000/cli to stale2000/git-sync because the repo name should match the project.
Entire stores checkpoint data in the Git branch entire/checkpoints/v1, not through a separate 'entire push' command.
The placeholder checkpoint remote github:org/checkpoints-repo is only a docs example and breaks expected same-repo checkpoint behavior if configured literally.
Entire's pre-push hook may push entire/checkpoints/v1 automatically, creating apparent ref-lock/race messages when an explicit push follows.
Installing Codex hooks mid-session may not capture the already-running session's SessionStart event; a new Codex process is cleaner for verification.

code.finding: Added regression coverage for legacy hosts.json direct map format accepted by the Entire local smoke helper.
Added a focused test proving envBoolDefault falls back to the provided default on invalid boolean environment values.
Entire Codex hooks were installed for SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, and Stop events.
Normal same-repo Entire settings should remain just enabled/telemetry without checkpoint_remote unless intentionally pushing checkpoints to a separate GitHub repo.

workflow: Normal Entire publishing flow is git commit followed by git push; prepare-commit-msg adds Entire-Checkpoint trailers and pre-push publishes entire/checkpoints/v1.
Synthetic hook calls can produce weak or empty checkpoints if transcript ordering is wrong; real codex exec better validates Codex agent integration.
entire session attach <session-id> --agent codex --force can directly attach a session to the current HEAD checkpoint.
CLI auth, browser auth, and web/search indexing are separate surfaces; CLI success does not prove the web UI is authenticated or indexed.

friction: Initial repo target was ambiguous: user first referenced stale2000/cli, then corrected to a new repo name.
mise trust warning appeared before local commands could run cleanly.
Codex hook trust had to be computed and added manually to ~/.codex/config.toml.
Synthetic smoke checkpoint initially had empty prompt/transcript data, so it was likely ignored by the web UI.
Commit messages created through shell quoting accidentally contained literal \n sequences and needed amend passes.
Explicit checkpoint pushes sometimes raced with Entire's pre-push helper, producing ref-lock/non-fast-forward style confusion even when the helper had already pushed.
In-app browser was initially unauthenticated to Entire web despite CLI auth being valid.
Entire web/search continued showing no checkpoints even after raw checkpoint files were verified on GitHub and browser auth was confirmed.
User accidentally configured checkpoint_remote to the placeholder github:org/checkpoints-repo, which had to be removed.
open_items: Investigate why Entire web/search does not discover or display checkpoints from stale2000/git-sync despite the pushed entire/checkpoints/v1 branch.
Attach the full desktop chat transcript explicitly using an empty commit plus entire session attach if the user wants this investigation preserved as a checkpoint.
Run the full go test ./... suite; only targeted internal/syncer tests were run during the session.
Confirm with Entire service maintainers or logs whether new repo checkpoint indexing requires a separate backend ingestion delay or repository registration step.
